title: Aspiration sites by position
claims: Upright: aspirate follows gravity into the basal segments of the lower lobes, right more than left.
The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and runs more vertically, so aspiration favors the right.
Supine: the dependent (posterior) segments fill first: the superior segment of the right lower lobe and the posterior segment of the right upper lobe.
Right lateral decubitus: the right lung is dependent, so aspirate favors its lateral and posterior regions.
The right lateral decubitus position is commonly taught less consistently than upright vs. supine: confirm the exact segments against your question-bank resource.
